Deterministic plans with zero variance enable reliable, reproducible agent behavior critical for production systems

whatToTry.description: If you're building agentic workflows (e.g., coding, web navigation), prototype a hybrid approach: use GATS's layered world model (symbolic + learned + LLM fallback) for planning, reserving LLM calls only for unknown actions. This can slash costs and improve reliability.

items.title: KV-PRM: 5000x Faster Process Reward Modeling for Multi-Agent AI
items.tldr: KV-PRM eliminates the quadratic cost of process reward modeling by reusing KV caches from LLM generation, achieving up to 5000x FLOP reduction and 37x latency improvement. This makes test-time scaling practical for long-context multi-agent systems.
whyItMatters: Enables real-time process reward feedback for long-horizon multi-agent tasks, unlocking more sophisticated agentic workflows without prohibitive compute costs.
Reduces memory footprint by 34x, allowing founders to deploy PRM-based TTS on smaller hardware or scale to larger agent teams.

whatToTry.description: If you're building multi-agent systems with test-time scaling (e.g., beam search, MCTS), prototype KV-PRM by extracting KV caches from your LLM's generation phase and using a single verify token for scoring. This can drastically cut inference costs for long trajectories.
whatToTry.note: Requires access to KV cache from the generation model; ensure your LLM framework supports cache extraction (e.g., Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM).

whatToTry.description: Experiment with a simple self-improvement loop: use an LLM to generate prompts or fine-tuning data, then evaluate and iterate on the output automatically. Start with a narrow task like code generation or content summarization.

Technical impact: Gaming data offers structured 3D environments and physics, enabling models to learn causality and spatial reasoning that text-only models lack.

items.title: First US autonomous ground vehicles deployed in Ukraine combat
items.tldr: Forterra has deployed over 100 autonomous ground vehicles in Ukraine, marking the first large-scale use of American self-driving military tech in active combat. This signals a major shift in defense AI and validates autonomous systems in high-stakes environments.
whyItMatters: Business impact: Opens a new market for defense AI startups; founders can explore government contracts for autonomous systems in logistics, surveillance, and combat support.

Technical impact: Proves that autonomous navigation and decision-making can function under extreme conditions (jamming, rough terrain, real-time threats), accelerating R&D for civilian applications like off-road delivery or disaster response.

whatToTry.description: Evaluate your AI product's robustness by stress-testing it against edge cases similar to combat scenarios—like sensor degradation, communication loss, or unpredictable environments. Consider partnering with defense or logistics firms to pilot autonomous systems in challenging conditions.
whatToTry.note: Start with simulation environments that mimic high-interference or low-visibility settings before real-world deployment.

items.title: iFLYTEK's Unified Omni Model for Embodied AI
items.tldr: iFLYTEK released a technical report on iFLYTEK-Embodied-Omni, a unified multimodal foundation model that jointly processes vision, language, and action for embodied agents. It uses a brain-cerebellum architecture to avoid cascading errors, combining visual-language reasoning, video generation, and action generation in a single framework, trained on a mix of human and robot data.
whyItMatters: For founders building robotics or embodied AI products, this model reduces pipeline complexity and error propagation by unifying perception, prediction, and action into one model, potentially enabling more robust long-horizon task execution.

The approach of combining action-annotated and action-free data for training could lower the barrier for developing general-purpose embodied agents, as it leverages diverse data sources including human demonstrations.

whatToTry.description: If you're developing an embodied AI system, evaluate whether a unified multimodal architecture (like iFLYTEK's) could replace your current cascaded pipeline. Start by testing the model's video generation and action generation on your specific tasks using the shared multimodal self-attention mechanism to see if it reduces error accumulation.
whatToTry.note: The model is still in research stage; consider replicating the data mixing strategy (action-annotated + action-free) to improve your own training datasets.

items.title: REDI: Open-Source Framework Automates Scientific Data Prep for AI
items.tldr: A new open-source framework, REDI, automates the five-stage pipeline of transforming raw scientific datasets into AI-ready training data, with built-in provenance tracking and agent-native deployment. This addresses a major bottleneck for founders building AI models in climate, proteomics, materials science, and fusion energy, and has demonstrated near-ideal scaling to 100 nodes on Frontier.
whyItMatters: Business impact: Reduces time and cost of data preparation for scientific AI startups, enabling faster iteration and deployment of domain-specific models.

Technical impact: Provides a standardized, reproducible pipeline with instrumentation, making it easier to scale data readiness across diverse scientific domains and integrate with agent-based systems.

whatToTry.description: Evaluate REDI for your scientific AI project by cloning the repository and testing it on a small sample of your raw dataset. Focus on the ingest and preprocess stages to see how it handles your data format, then use the provenance tracking to identify I/O bottlenecks and optimize format selection.
whatToTry.note: Start with a single domain (e.g., climate data) to minimize complexity, and leverage SetGo for FAIR compliance if you plan to publish datasets.

sources.title: Automated Data Readiness for Scientific AI

items.title: SwarmResearch: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Open-Ended Discovery
items.tldr: A new paper introduces SwarmResearch, an orchestrator-subagent harness that uses a Shepherd Agent to steer multiple Search Agents in separate git branches, avoiding convergence on single approaches and achieving better solutions on 13/15 open-ended optimization tasks.
whyItMatters: Improves AI agent efficiency for complex, open-ended coding tasks by preventing premature convergence on suboptimal solutions.
Demonstrates a scalable multi-agent architecture that adapts parallelism dynamically, potentially reducing compute costs while improving outcomes.

whatToTry.description: Implement a similar orchestrator-subagent pattern in your AI coding workflows: use a 'shepherd' agent to monitor multiple parallel agents working in isolated branches, periodically evaluating and recombining their best approaches to avoid local optima.
whatToTry.note: Start with simple tasks like code optimization or bug fixing to test the pattern before scaling to complex projects.

items.title: MedCalc-Pro: LLM Agents Tackle Complex Medical Calculations
items.tldr: A new benchmark and agent framework for LLMs in medical calculations, moving beyond single-calculator tasks to multi-calculator and nested scenarios, with a proposed method that outperforms existing models.
whyItMatters: For founders building AI in healthcare, this highlights the need for multi-tool orchestration and error suppression in real-world clinical workflows, opening opportunities for agent-based solutions.
Technically, the structured validation and evidence review approach offers a blueprint for improving LLM reliability in high-stakes domains like medicine.

whatToTry.description: Evaluate your own medical AI agent against the MedCalc-Pro benchmark to identify gaps in multi-calculator and nested-calculator reasoning, then implement structured validation to reduce error propagation.
whatToTry.note: The framework is generalizable; consider adapting it for other regulated industries requiring multi-step calculations.

items.title: Oyster-II: RL for Safer, More Helpful LLMs
items.tldr: Oyster-II uses reinforcement learning to improve LLM safety alignment, moving beyond blanket refusals to constructive responses. It outperforms Qwen3-14B and matches Qwen3-Max on safety, addressing over-generalization issues in prior SFT-based methods.
whyItMatters: For founders building AI products, this approach reduces the risk of LLMs refusing legitimate user queries, improving user experience and trust.
Technically, it demonstrates that RL-based alignment can achieve cross-scale safety performance comparable to much larger models, potentially reducing compute costs.

whatToTry.description: Evaluate your current LLM's refusal patterns on sensitive but legitimate queries (e.g., health, finance). If over-refusal is an issue, consider fine-tuning with a constructive safety dataset or experimenting with RL-based alignment techniques like those in Oyster-II.
whatToTry.note: Start with small-scale tests on domain-specific queries before full deployment.

items.title: VERITAS: AI tool automates scientific replication, boosts research integrity
items.tldr: VERITAS is a new domain-agnostic AI framework that automates replication of scientific research by extracting claims, running experiments, and scoring reproducibility. It outperforms baselines across 65 papers in CS, medicine, and astrophysics, addressing a critical bottleneck in scientific integrity.
whyItMatters: For founders building AI products in research or compliance, VERITAS demonstrates a scalable approach to automated verification, opening opportunities for tools that audit AI-generated outputs or validate scientific claims.

Technically, it shows how CLI coding agents can be generalized beyond benchmarks, reducing the cost and time of replication from months to hours, which could accelerate product development in regulated industries.

whatToTry.description: Explore integrating VERITAS-like claim extraction and automated testing into your AI product pipeline. For example, if you build AI for scientific writing or code generation, consider adding a replication-check module that validates outputs against stated claims.
whatToTry.note: Start with small-scale experiments on open-source papers to gauge accuracy before scaling to proprietary data.

items.tldr: Fans are using generative AI tools to create and spread hyper-realistic, humorous videos and images of footballer Erling Haaland, demonstrating how AI is enabling new forms of user-generated content and viral internet culture.

items.title: Internal Pluralism: Why AI Alignment Needs More Than Pairwise Comparisons
items.tldr: A new paper reveals that pairwise comparisons—a common tool for learning human preferences in AI alignment—fail under internal pluralism, where individuals hold multiple conflicting priorities. Allowing indecision reduces queries and improves accuracy, challenging current RLHF practices.
whyItMatters: Business impact: Founders building AI products with human feedback loops (e.g., RLHF) may be using flawed methods that miss global preferences like fairness, leading to misaligned outputs and user distrust.

Technical impact: The paper provides a formal model showing that forced local comparisons can distort learning, and suggests allowing indecision as a more efficient alternative—potentially reducing data needs and improving model alignment.

whatToTry.description: Audit your preference collection pipeline: If you use pairwise comparisons for RLHF or user feedback, pilot a version that includes an 'undecided' or 'skip' option. Measure if this reduces the number of queries needed to converge on accurate preferences, especially for tasks involving fairness or trade-offs.
whatToTry.note: This is early-stage research; test on small-scale user studies before full deployment.

sources.title: Internal Pluralism and the Limits of Pairwise Comparisons

items.title: ASK+ Boosts SLM Guidance in Partial Observability RL
items.tldr: A new paper reveals that small language models (SLMs) can effectively guide reinforcement learning agents under partial observability when given trajectory-aware context and chain-of-thought reasoning, achieving up to 17% success gains over vanilla methods.
whyItMatters: For founders building AI agents or robotics systems, this shows how to leverage small, cost-efficient models for decision-making in real-world scenarios with incomplete information, reducing reliance on expensive large models.

The insight that predictive entropy measures action uncertainty (not state uncertainty) enables practical uncertainty-gated assistance, making SLM integration viable for POMDPs common in autonomous systems.

whatToTry.description: When integrating SLMs into your agent pipeline, replace bare prompts with trajectory-aware context: include partial observations, action history, and visited states. Use structured chain-of-thought reasoning to convert the SLM from a passive checker into an active consultant, and gate its interventions on action uncertainty (predictive entropy) rather than state uncertainty.
whatToTry.note: Start with a simple environment like DoorKey to test the approach before scaling to complex tasks.

sources.title: ASK in the Dark: Uncertainty-Gated LLM Assistance under Partial Observability
